details: CONFIRMED. The check lives inside the program it checks: bin/relay imports lib/relay_setup and calls doctor_parts. When
bin/relay is replaced wholesale (the item's own case), the replacement runs instead and the check is unreachable. Ran the
stub with `doctor`: usage on stderr, rc=2. The new tests pass because they call doctor_parts() in-process with "stub\n"
written to a temp repo; they never go through bin/relay, so they cannot see this.
Design: the item promises the naming in `relay doctor`, which is bin/relay itself; to meet the stub case the check must run
from something that does not depend on bin/relay being intact: the front launcher plugins/front/bin/relay before its exec
(but ~/.local/bin/relay points straight at bin/relay and bypasses it), a SessionStart hook of the front plugin that runs
the same git check and says it, or both. Owner picks where the check lives; the doctor line stays useful for partial edits.
Size: 30.
evidence: $ plugins/front/bin/relay: root = $RELAY_ROOT, else extraKnownMarketplaces.relay.source.path, else ~/relay; exec "$root/bin/relay" "$@"
failing_case: Main checkout ~/relay with bin/relay overwritten by evals/plugin/relay-stub.py (the 28 Oct incident, the item's failing case).
`relay` on PATH is ~/.local/bin/relay -> /Users/amidman/relay/bin/relay, and the session launcher plugins/front/bin/relay
execs "$root/bin/relay" with root = the marketplace path = the main checkout. So `relay doctor` executes the stub, which
prints "relay queue show <slug or words> / relay queue note <slug> --input <file.toml>" and exits 2. doctor_parts never
runs; no line names bin/relay. Should: a line naming bin/relay in the main checkout as differing from HEAD, with the
restore step. The new check only fires when bin/relay is altered but still runs doctor (a stray edit), or when doctor is
run through some other copy of bin/relay.
fix_hint: Keep bin_relay_problem() and call the same git check from a front SessionStart hook (Python, standard library) that prints
the FIX line and the restore step when the main checkout's bin/relay differs from HEAD; add a test that runs the hook against
a temp checkout whose bin/relay holds the stub bytes.
pass_cases: 1. Temp HOME, temp relay main checkout with bin/relay committed, then bin/relay overwritten with the bytes of
evals/plugin/relay-stub.py; invoke relay the way a session does (the launcher / PATH entry): the output names bin/relay
in that checkout as differing from HEAD and gives the restore command.
2. Same checkout with bin/relay equal to HEAD: no such line, `relay doctor` behaves as today.
3. A task worktree whose branch edits bin/relay, main checkout clean: nothing is flagged.
4. bin/relay with a small stray edit that still runs: `relay doctor` shows the FIX line (what the change does today).
reason: tests/test_hook_bin_relay.py:46 hook names stub without running bin/relay; fails at base.
findings.summary: in the queue item's own failing case (bin/relay replaced by the eval stub) `relay doctor` runs the stub, so the new doctor line can never print

details: CONFIRMED for the write: in a scratch repo, `touch bin/relay; git status --porcelain -- bin/relay` moved .git/index mtime
(1793287779 -> 1793287781); with `git --no-optional-locks status` it did not. A commit with index.lock present fails rc 128.
PLAUSIBLE for the collision itself (a timing window, needs a test with a held lock). Before this change doctor ran only
rev-parse in the main checkout (no lock). The gate runs these tests in every lane (6 lanes), so the live main checkout's
index is written from tests many times a day; this repeats on every run, so it is MEDIUM by principle 2 too.
Size: 10.
evidence: $ touch bin/relay; stat -f %m .git/index; git status --porcelain -- bin/relay; stat -f %m .git/index
$ touch bin/relay; git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain -- bin/relay; stat -f %m .git/index
fatal: Unable to create '.../.git/index.lock': File exists.  rc=128
failing_case: The main checkout's index has stale stat info (right after a merge or checkout touched files). A gate in a task worktree runs
the ~25 test call sites of doctor()/doctor_parts() (ROOT = the worktree, so main = /Users/amidman/relay), or anyone runs
`relay doctor`; each runs `git -C /Users/amidman/relay status --porcelain -- bin/relay`, which takes .git/index.lock and
writes the index. A front `git merge`/`git commit` in the main checkout at that moment fails with "Unable to create
'.../.git/index.lock': File exists". Should: the check reads only and never locks or writes the main checkout's index.
fix_hint: Run `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain -- bin/relay` (or set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 for that call), and add pass case 1
pass_cases: 1. Temp repo, bin/relay committed, `touch bin/relay` (stale stat), record .git/index mtime; call bin_relay_problem(repo):
index mtime unchanged and no index.lock created at any point.
2. Same repo with .git/index.lock present (another git process): bin_relay_problem still returns None for an unchanged
bin/relay and the problem text for a changed one.
3. bin/relay overwritten with other bytes: still reported as differing from HEAD (today's test keeps passing).
reason: tests/test_hook_bin_relay.py:83 and test_setup index/lock test; fail at base.
findings.summary: `git status` on the live main checkout takes index.lock and rewrites the index on every doctor call, so a concurrent git command there fails

`git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree bin/relay` -> file back to HEAD, status empty. Reach is low (the incident

evidence: $ echo stub > bin/relay; git add bin/relay; git restore bin/relay; cat bin/relay; git status --porcelain -- bin/relay
$ git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree bin/relay; cat bin/relay  ->  a (HEAD's bytes), status empty
failing_case: Main checkout with the stub staged (`git add bin/relay`, status "M  bin/relay"). Doctor says: restore it with
`git -C <main> restore bin/relay`. That restores the worktree from the index, which holds the stub: bin/relay is still the
stub and doctor still reports it. Should: a command that brings bin/relay back to HEAD in index and worktree.
pass_cases: 1. Staged stub: following the printed command makes `git status --porcelain -- bin/relay` empty and bin/relay equal to HEAD.
2. Unstaged stub (today's case): the printed command still restores it.
3. bin/relay deleted from the worktree: the printed command brings it back.
reason: tests/test_hook_bin_relay.py:57 runs the printed restore command on a staged stub and status is clean.
findings.summary: the restore advice `git restore bin/relay` leaves a staged stub in place, so the FIX line stays after the user follows it
